title: Advanced Factoring: Non-Monic Trinomials and Cubes
description: Factor non-monic trinomials with organized factor-pair trials, then apply sum- and difference-of-cubes patterns, including GCF and sign variations.

questions.stem_html: Which choice gives the complete factorization of \(6x^{2}+13x+6\) over the integers?
questions.explanation_html: After the GCF 1, choose leading factors 2 and 3. The cross-products add to 13 and the constants multiply to 6. Expanding \((2x+3)(3x+2)\) checks the result.
questions.variation: Choose, Arrange, Match for a non-monic trinomial

distractor_notes.A: Swaps the constant placements and changes the middle products.
distractor_notes.B: Flips both signs, changing the middle coefficient.
distractor_notes.D: Changes a constant so the product no longer matches.

questions.stem_html: Which choice gives the complete factorization of \(x^3-27\) over the integers?
questions.explanation_html: Remove any common factor first. The cube roots are \(x\) and \(3\). Keep the original sign in the linear factor, reverse it in the middle term, and keep the final square positive. The complete factorization is \((x-3)(x^2+3x+9)\).

distractor_notes.A: Keeps the same sign in the middle of the quadratic.
